correctness.rationale: For all n>=3, the normalized cosine eigenvector has y^T P y-c equal to a nonnegative diagonal slack with strictly positive interior coefficients. The spectral-norm bound y^T P^2 y<=s(P)^2 gives the squared energy inequality. Every equality case must have zero interior hold, hence alternating edge weights. Pairwise cosine-mode diagonalization proves that the alternating family attains equality and gives its exact spectrum. Summation and centered Cauchy--Schwarz derive coordinate recovery. All endpoint and degenerate t=+/-1/2 cases are covered algebraically. The supplied verifier independently passed 4,899 test matrices; finite tests are not the infinite proof.

Originality is limited to evidence actually inspected; unindexed equivalences remain possible.

value.rationale: A fixed-width path is a canonical load-balancing and Markov-chain optimization model. The sharp global quadratic remainder distinguishes all near-optimal transition rules, recovers individual edge probabilities from observable SLEM excess, classifies the complete equality family for a nontrivial stability inequality, and proves that square-root recovery is unavoidable. This is not the already-known unperturbed optimal probability assignment, a finite sample, or a numerical table.
